linkedin.post:
19 of 38. That is how many David Jones stores its receivers plan to close, with closures expected by the end of the year.

The 188-year-old retailer went into administration last week after rent talks with Westfield owner Scentre broke down. Scentre says no rent was paid from 30 September. Receivers FTI Consulting say the cuts give David Jones "the best chance for a sustainable future". Barrenjoey's Tom Kierath expects any comeback to be "much smaller". Buyers have until Friday.

If half of David Jones closes to save the rest, is that a rescue or just a slower goodbye?

Tell us what you think below.

warnings: Wikimedia Commons refused downloads from the cloud address all run (HTTP 429), so the video has no genuine photos of David Jones stores; every shot is generic licensed department-store or shopping-centre file footage, labelled 'File footage' on screen.
Job losses from the 19 closures have not been published; the video and posts give no figure. 'About 6,000' is David Jones's total workforce (ABC) and is not used as a job-loss number.

Receivers are FTI Consulting (appointed by the secured lender); the voluntary administrator is McGrathNicol, which set the Fri 13 Nov deadline for expressions of interest. Some reports blur the two roles.
'Rent unpaid since 30 September' and 'under $100 million' purchase price are from Scentre Group and The Nightly (5 Nov) respectively; Anchorage has not confirmed the price.
Tom Kierath's quote is partial: 'If it does come back, it will come back in a much smaller, slimline version…' (ABC News, 11 Nov).
